name: umask
summary: Sets the permissions removed by default from new files.
description: Shell builtin. The mask says which permissions to remove when a file is created: a file starts from 666 and a directory from 777, then the bits of the mask are removed. With the common mask 022, files are created as 644 (rw-r--r--) and directories as 755. The change only lasts for the current session; to make it permanent, add it to ~/.bashrc.

options.description: Prints or accepts the mask in symbolic form: the permissions that are kept (u=rwx,g=rx,o=rx).
Prints the mask in a form that can be reused as a command.

arguments.name: MASK
arguments.description: New mask in octal (022, 077) or symbolic form (u=rwx,g=,o=). Without an argument, prints the current mask.

examples.explanation: The same mask, expressed as the permissions that are kept.
Files created afterwards will only be accessible to you (600 for a file, 700 for a directory).
